events.text: You are practising alone at dusk, and the lamp throws your shadow on the yard wall. You lift your arm, and the shadow is slow to lift its own. It is also a good deal bigger than the wall has any right to hold. {dhf_Form} has come to stand behind you: {dhf_look}, thin as smoke in a shut room. Nobody ever told you this was possible. Nobody at your rung is left to ask.

choices.text: Turn around and look at it

effects.log: You turn around. There is nothing behind you but the yard and the evening. When you turn back it is on the wall, waiting. You sleep very little, and in the morning your stance is better than it has ever been.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on the form you were practising

effects.log: You finish the whole set, every move, with your back to it. When you lower your hands, you feel it lower its own. It seems to approve of that. In your next fight, you will know it is there.

events.text: The bell has gone for the middle watch and you are alone in the Hall of Arhats, sweeping between the five hundred statues as you have since you were nineteen. The dust is lit with a colour there is no lamp for. All five hundred have turned their eyes a little to the left, to the place just behind your shoulder. You know what you will see if you turn: old gold, and a face of great patience.

choices.text: Put down the broom and bow to it

effects.log: You bow. It does not bow back. It looks past you at the door, the way a thing looks at a door it is responsible for. In the morning you tell no one, and everyone looks at you a little oddly anyway.

choices.text: Go on sweeping

effects.log: You go on sweeping. It seems to you that is the correct answer, or at least that no one is going to mark you down. By the end of the row, the colour has faded, and the floor is very clean.

events.text: An old woman with paint under her nails sits down across from you at the noodle stall. She is Geum Seokhwa, she says, sixty-one years a painter of temple banners. "I only ever painted what stood behind people. Most have a shape about as big as a hen." She looks over your shoulder and up, and goes on looking up. "Sit still. I have never done one this size. It will take me a month."

choices.text: Sit for her

effects.log: You sit for a month in a shed that smells of glue and ground malachite. She works with her back to you and never once looks at your face. When she unrolls it you do not say anything for some time. You understand now how far it can reach.

choices.text: Tell her it is no one's business

effects.log: "It is not," she agrees, and finishes her noodles. "It will not stop being there, you know. I will be at the dye-works by the river until the snow." She leaves you with her bill, and you pay it.

events.text: Elder Wolgong of the Hall of Arhats walks you to the lower gate, slowly, being ninety. "It is not yours," he says at last. "Nobody ever earned a guardian. A gate needs keeping, and you happen to be standing in it." He pats the old gatepost as he would a horse. "Those who think it is theirs begin to use it for things. You will see what it looks like when it does not like something."

choices.text: Ask him what it is for, then

effects.log: "I sweep, and you ask," he says. "One of us is going to be disappointed." But he stays until the evening bell and answers a little of it, sideways, and you carry that up the mountain.

choices.text: Ask him if he has one

effects.log: He laughs until he has to hold the post. "I had a cough for forty years and a bad knee for thirty," he says. "The temple has had one in your generation, and one in my teacher's. I carried the water for him." He looks pleased about that, entirely.

events.text: It was only a sparring match behind the granary. But a carter on the ridge road saw your shape go up against the evening, and he has told it at three inns, taller each time. By the end of the month people you have never met are leaving things at your gate: rice, a live goose, a sick child held out at arm's length by a mother who does not quite dare to knock.

choices.text: Open the gate and do what you can

effects.log: You do what you can, and it is not what they came for. The goose stays. The child gets better on its own, as children do, and now that is also a thing that is said about you.

choices.text: Have the gate barred, and move on before winter

effects.log: You are three provinces away by the first snow, and this time you practise indoors. There is a certain relief in being nobody. It lasts until the next carter.

choices.text: Let them say it. Fear is a fence

effects.log: You say nothing and let it grow. People stop trying your door. They stop trying a good many other things, too, and there is a whole street now that goes quiet when you walk down it.

events.text: You come round the wall and find eleven novices on their faces in the wet leaves. One of them saw it behind you at dawn drill. The youngest, a sharp-boned child called Haeun, is whispering something and getting it wrong. Elder Wolgong watches from the kitchen door with a bowl in his hand. He is not going to help. He looks as if he has been waiting years to see what you do.

choices.text: Pick up a broom and start on the leaves around them

effects.log: You sweep around them, one at a time, with some care. One by one they get up and find something else to do. Only Haeun stays down the longest, and then comes and takes the other broom. From the kitchen door, you hear someone eating soup with satisfaction.

choices.text: Tell them plainly to stand up: this is not to be knelt to

effects.log: They stand, ashamed. It will be years before any of them looks you in the eye, and you have the feeling it was the right thing, done a little too loud. The Elder says only, "Hm."

choices.text: Let them finish. It will do discipline no harm

effects.log: You stand and let them finish. They do it very well. Something at your back shifts its weight, and for the rest of that day the gold does not come to you when you look for it.

events.text: You see your form again in a market town, hanging from a pole, for sale. It is not Geum Seokhwa's hand: it has the proportions of a fat tax collector, and it is the fifth you have counted this year. The seller swears it wards off fever. Geum's true banner has gone, bought by a rich family and robbed by a richer. Everyone has a price now on a thing only you ever had to carry.

choices.text: Buy every bad copy on the stall and burn them

effects.log: It costs you a good deal of silver and teaches the seller that there is a market. Next spring there are twice as many, and the fat one has a sword now.

choices.text: Track the true banner down, and take it back

ok.log: It takes you a year and a bribe. It is rolled up in a strongbox, and nobody has dared to hang it. You bring it back to Geum, who looks it over for damp. "It is better than I remember," she says, and goes back to work.

fail.log: You find the house, then a second house, then a story about a fire. The banner is gone. In time you come to think it may be better that nobody knows what it can reach.

choices.text: Leave them to it. People want a fever ward

effects.log: You walk on. A woman buys the fat one for her son, and in the end you decide that it may do him as much good as anything else in this province.

events.text: Geum Seokhwa has found you, as old painters do, and has painted it anyway, from what the carters say and one look across a river. It hangs in a roadside shrine with the paint still tacky, wrong in nine places, and you cannot stop looking at it. "I could only guess at the reach," she says. "Sit for me and I'll correct it. Or they can pray to my mistakes. They will never know."

choices.text: Sit for her now

effects.log: A month in the glue shed. She corrects all nine, and tells you about each of them, and you learn more about your own shoulders than you have from thirty years of teachers.

choices.text: Tell her to leave it wrong

effects.log: "Good," she says. "Somebody will come to look for that one, and you will see them coming." She packs up her brushes. You think she may be right, and you find you hope so.

events.text: Seven men come to the mountain gate with a dying friend and someone else's silver, and half a day behind them, the magistrate's cavalry. The law says hand them over. The Rule says no one in need is turned away. When the horses come up the road you are the one standing in the gate, and you feel it rise unasked. It looks down the road with no opinion at all. It only will not move.

choices.text: Stand in the gate until the captain turns back, and give up the silver yourself

effects.log: The captain looks up and up, and his horse will not come on. You send the silver down with a novice and a list. The seven are gone by spring. Nobody writes it in the temple record, but the local magistrate writes to the abbot at length.

choices.text: Step aside. Let the law come in and look

effects.log: You step aside and it does too, without complaint, which surprises you. Three of the seven hang. The dying one dies on the way to the town. You sit up that night, and nobody tells you that you were wrong, and nobody tells you that you were right.

choices.text: Go down the road and meet the captain's blade yourself

ok.log: You put him on his back, gently, with all his men watching, and you sit by him until he can ride. It is an entirely unnecessary victory. It will be told against the temple for years.

fail.log: He is better than he looks. You come back up the road on a borrowed horse, and the gate has stayed shut behind you the whole time. It did not need you for that.

events.text: Your household keeps odd hours now. A pot gets moved off the east wall. The cook will not go through the back room after dark. Then the youngest asks you at supper, in a clear voice, why the tall person never sits down, and everyone stops eating. It has been behind you all this time, even at home. You had thought only you could feel it. You have been very lonely in a very full house.

choices.text: Move your bed out to the shed, for now

effects.log: You move out to the shed. The cook goes back through the back room. It is quite peaceful, and you can hear them all laughing from there, some evenings.

choices.text: Sit down with them and let the little one ask it things

effects.log: It does not answer, of course. But the youngest takes to putting out a bowl for it, and the others laugh at that and then stop laughing and get used to it. It is not nothing, to be got used to.

choices.text: Tell them it is none of their concern

effects.log: You say it pleasantly, and that is worse. They take care after that never to ask you anything else.

events.text: Haeun, grown long-armed and argumentative, catches you on the woodpile. "I have read the Hall's records. The Guardian keeps out the unworthy. So. Are you worthy? Or is it keeping you out too, and you can't see which side of the gate you're on?" The novice is holding an axe rather carelessly, is very nearly crying, and has obviously not slept.

choices.text: "I don't know which side. Hold the axe by the end"

effects.log: Haeun looks at the axe, and starts laughing, and then is crying, and then you split wood together until the bell. You do not think you have ever been asked a better question.

choices.text: Tell the truth: you have never once felt worthy

effects.log: Haeun nods for a while. "Elder Wolgong says that is what they all say," the novice says. "He also said the ones who say it are insufferable." You will be some time getting over that.

choices.text: Send the novice to the Elder for this kind of thing

effects.log: You send Haeun away, rather shortly, and you have an uneasy feeling afterwards of having been the sort of person a gate is there to stop.

events.text: Dal, the apprentice, a square and silent person who has ground colour for Geum Seokhwa since the age of eight, brings a message that took two winters to come. She is ninety-four and nearly blind. She wants to see it, one time, at its whole height, and then she will have seen everything there was. Dal holds out a travelling-paper and a very small bag of silver.

choices.text: Go. Raise it in the yard at the dye-works, as high as it will go

effects.log: She sits in a chair in the frost with her face turned up. You give it everything you have got. The whole town comes out on its roofs. "Hm," she says, after a long time. "The left shoulder. I always knew." She dies that spring, still correcting it. You carry a corner of the bier, and Dal keeps the brushes.

choices.text: Send Dal back with silver and a letter, you cannot get away

effects.log: You write a good letter. The silver buys her a warm winter. Dal comes back the next autumn to return your letter, unopened, since she could not have read it. Dal does not reproach you. You would feel better if Dal did.

choices.text: Go, but go quietly, and raise it by night, for her alone

effects.log: The town sleeps through it. She cannot see it really, in the dark, with those eyes. But she takes hold of your sleeve and turns her face to it exactly, and says, "There you are," and you do not know which of you she is speaking to.

events.text: Elder Wolgong has stopped getting up. They carry him to the east porch so he can tell the novices they are sweeping wrong. At evening he looks over your shoulder, for the first time in all these years, and his eyes stay there. "So," he says, "that's what it looks like from this side." Later: "Who keeps the gate when you're gone? I carried water for one. You find someone to carry water."

choices.text: Bring Haeun, and give the novice the water bucket

effects.log: He looks at Haeun, and at the bucket, and laughs until the infirmarian is sent for. He dies before the snow. Haeun carries water for you for the next nine years and never once stops arguing, and you never tell anyone why.

choices.text: Stay with him through the night, and let the gold stand over the porch

effects.log: Nobody told you that you could. It stands all night, as tall as the bell tower, and it does nothing whatever. In the morning, the novices find the Elder asleep, and then not. They find the dust on the porch swept.

choices.text: Ask him, at last, if you were worthy

effects.log: "You asked," he says, delighted. "They all ask. I told the abbot you would." He seems to go to sleep on that, and he does not wake up, and you have to go on not knowing, as he must have known that you would.

events.text: Dal has gone on painting. You hear of it from a mountain shrine, then a ferry-post: small square banners, dry and sure, of what stands behind people no one looks at. A salt-carrier, a midwife, an old soldier who sweeps a bridge. Most have a shape the size of a hen. At the last shrine you find a tall shape seen from very far off, a smudge on a ridge, with the left shoulder correct.

choices.text: Leave silver at the shrine, for the next banner

effects.log: You leave what you have got. Dal takes no pupils and answers no letters. But there is a banner of a ferry-woman, later on, that has been done on very good silk.

choices.text: Go and find Dal, and sit for a true one

effects.log: You find Dal grinding blue on a step. Dal looks at you, and past you, and shakes a square head. "Done that," Dal says. "Doing the bridge-sweeper. You can hold the shell." You hold the shell for a week and are happier than you were in the Tournament.

choices.text: Stand on the bridge a while, looking at the old soldier sweep

effects.log: He has got a shape about the size of a hen. It sweeps when he sweeps. You have raised yours against masters who shook the sky, and you stand there for an hour and do not feel that you are any taller.

events.text: You did not train for it. A morning comes and you can tell before you open your eyes that {dhf_form} is standing further off than it was and is taller, the way you can tell a mountain is there in fog. It is {dhf_size} now. The pines on the near ridge have started to grow slightly away from your house. Masters you have outlived would have given their teeth for this. There is nobody to tell.

choices.text: Climb the ridge and stand beside it

effects.log: You climb all morning and it is no closer to being beside you. But you can see a very long way from up there, and it seems to want you to look.

choices.text: Go on with the day. There is wood to split

effects.log: You split the wood. It watches. There is, as far as you can tell, a certain respect in it.

events.text: It is night, you are not in a good way, and {dhf_form} is looking at you. It has always looked ahead. You have seen that look in a bad mirror, at the end of a long bad year. It asks for nothing. But you can tell, the way a rider can, that it would go a great deal faster if you loosened the rein, and that it is tired of who you have been pretending to be.

choices.text: Loosen the rein

effects.log: You loosen it. You hear it breathe in, all the way down, for the first time. Nothing has ever been so easy. You sleep very well, and in the morning there is frost on the side of the house it stands on.

choices.text: Sit up with it until morning, and do not look away

effects.log: You sit it out. It takes all night, and something tears in your chest that does not heal for a month. In the grey hour it goes back to looking ahead, as if nothing had happened.

events.text: The novices have stopped bringing your bowl. At drill the gold came when you called and it was the wrong gold, the colour of a coin long in a bad hand. In the Hall, all five hundred statues have their eyes on the opposite wall. You can feel the Guardian's patience, a great way up, and it is the patience it has for whatever is on the wrong side of a door.

choices.text: Let it be iron, then. A gate can be held by iron

effects.log: You go on. The gold darkens and it gets stronger. It stops raising one open hand and starts to raise a closed one. Nobody at the temple says anything at all, and that is how you know.

choices.text: Go down to the Hall and kneel until they look at you

effects.log: You kneel for nine days. The novices step round you. On the tenth morning there is a bowl beside your knee, and one statue at the end of the row, a small one with a chipped ear, has turned its eyes a little your way.

events.text: Dogs will not stay on your street now. A stall-holder you have bought from for years gives you your change without looking up, and it is not you he is afraid to look at. {dhf_Form} stands closer than it did, and it has started to lean. Some nights you feel that if you lay down and stopped paying attention, it would quite like to find out what it could do on its own.

choices.text: Walk the bounds at night, and let it see that you are still here

effects.log: You walk till dawn, every night for a month. It is like walking a large dog on a thin string, and you are both aware of the string.

choices.text: Let it lean. You like the quiet on your street

effects.log: It leans. The street is very quiet. It occurs to you some time later that you cannot remember when you last heard anyone laugh on it.

events.text: You wake in the morning and something is wrong, and you lie there for a time working out what. It is the birds. There are birds again. {dhf_Form} stands where it has always stood, looking ahead. There is a mark on it, faint, like the line a flood leaves on a wall, and you think that will stay. Otherwise it is only tall. You had forgotten that it could be only tall. You go out and buy a dog, for no reason.

choices.text: Tell someone. Anyone

effects.log: You tell the woman who sells you the dog. She has no idea what you are talking about, and says, "That's good, then," and you find to your surprise that you have to sit down.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be careful from now on

effects.log: You say nothing and you are careful. You will go on being careful for the rest of your life, and it does not feel like a burden, exactly. It feels like knowing where the step is in the dark.

events.text: They got you home somehow. You remember the fight, up to the moment when you raised it, and then you remember a very clear view of the sky from the ground, and something enormous standing over you with its back to your enemy. It had not been looking at them for some time. It stands in your room now as you try to breathe. It is entirely calm. It wants you to know that it could have gone on.

choices.text: Tell it, out loud, that you are still the one who decides

effects.log: Your voice is not much. It listens, or it does not. But when you can stand again, it stands where it did before and a little further back, and you have got a long way to go.

choices.text: Laugh. You would have done the same

effects.log: You laugh, and it hurts. You have an impression, very far up, that you have said the right thing, and that this is not at all good news.

events.text: The snow has stopped halfway down the pass. {npc} stands at the top, alone, and behind {him} stands {dhf_rival}, enormous and familiar, the way a tune is when you cannot remember the words. "I wondered if you would get one," {he} says. "I got mine the year you got yours. It took me a while to stop laughing." Yours has already risen, unasked. They have seen each other.

choices.text: Let the two of them meet, and end it

ok.log: It takes a long time and the whole province sees it. {dhf_Form} stands. The other sinks down through the air like a tower going into a lake. {npc} is on {his} knees in the snow. "So that's how it ends," {he} says, and bows to the ground. "I will not be born beside you again." The knot is cut.

fail.log: {dhf_Form} goes down on one knee in the pass. The thing behind {npc} leans over you and stops. So does {npc}. "Not yet," {he} says, breathing hard. "Not with those eyes. Find me again."

choices.text: Turn yours away, and walk up to {him} with your hands empty

mem.note: turned away a form in the pass

effects.log: {dhf_Form} goes down by degrees, with bad grace, as a very large dog sits. The other stays up a while longer. Then {npc} sits on a rock and laughs and says, "Well, that is a terrible thing to do to someone." The knot is not untied. But it is a good deal looser, and you have until you are both ready.

choices.text: "Not this year"

effects.log: "No," {npc} agrees, looking up at the two of them. "They would break the pass." {He} shoulders {his} pack. "I have waited lives. I can wait for you to get taller."

events.text: You had thought that was all finished. {npc} turns up at your gate in the spring, older, with a stick {he} does not need. There is no knot left, and nothing to settle between you. {He} looks up over your shoulder. "I never got to see them meet properly," {he} says. "I was busy. Mine has been sulking for years. It would like to see yours, if you have an afternoon. Nothing in it, for anyone."

choices.text: Go up to the high meadow and let them have it out

ok.log: Afterwards you lie in the flattened grass, side by side, too tired to say who won. Over the valley, the two great shapes stand and look at the view. {npc} says, "It likes you better than I do," and you say, "It has always been a poor judge."

fail.log: It is a very good afternoon, and you lose it. {npc} is insufferable all the way down the mountain and stays a month, and you find you have to invent reasons for {him} to leave and then forget them.

choices.text: Sit on the step with {him} instead, and let them stand behind you

effects.log: You sit on the step. Neither of you calls anything. But around sunset, you notice that the long shadows on the road have stopped being two.

events.text: Other children cast small shadows and do not mind them. You keep looking behind you. There is never anything there, and the grown-ups have stopped asking. But you always leave room. You duck under gates a head too high. A very old woman selling paint at the fair looks at you for a long moment, and then, for no reason, gives you a shell of blue.

choices.text: Keep the shell

effects.log: You keep it for years, without knowing why. It is an extremely good blue.

choices.text: Ask her what she saw

effects.log: She looks you over. "Nothing yet," she says. "Eat more." You think about that for a long time.

events.text: Understanding {dhf_form} comes as a language comes: you were following it for a long time, and then you are simply listening. When you open your eyes at the isle's edge, the cloud-sea below has a dent in it, and the dent is your shadow. Behind you stands {dhf_look}. An old immortal drifting by on a raft of cloud sets down her pipe and steers, without comment, for somewhere else.

choices.text: Ask it what it is

effects.log: It is the Dao, looking at you as you have looked at it. It does not answer. You have the odd impression that you have just been told something, and that it will take you a century to hear it.

choices.text: Stand up and walk to the far side of the isle, to see if it comes

effects.log: It comes. It does not walk, exactly. The isle tips by the width of a hair as it goes, and all the immortals who keep their teacups on the sill take them down.

events.text: You came up through the clouds carrying a thing thin as smoke, and you thought it the most terrible thing in the world. On the first clear morning on the Isles, {dhf_form} stands at your back, {dhf_size}, waiting to be told what to be. The immortals of the isle are polite. "Oh, you brought yours with you," one says. "From down there. How touching. Mine came with a bill."

choices.text: Ask what kind of a bill

effects.log: She tells you about the Register of Forms and the Jade Court's Recorder, in some detail, with relish. You will be hearing from them. She seems to look forward to it.

choices.text: Say nothing and look at her form instead

effects.log: You look. There is, you realise, a very great deal of it, stacked up behind the pleasant face, and it has been looking at you since you landed. You bow. So does she, not at all as deeply.

events.text: Nobody here knows what it is. They have Sword-Spirits and Pale Giants on these isles, and something that eats weather. Then you walk the Jade Road with a guardian at your back in dusty gold, its open hand raised, and the rafts stop. "What does it do?" asks a child of nine hundred. "It seems to be stopping something." It is looking past you, as ever, at a door no one else can see.

choices.text: Say that you do not know what it is stopping

effects.log: The child nods gravely. "My mother says all the worst ones are like that," the child says. You will think about that one.

choices.text: Find a quiet place and build it a gate, out of driftwood

effects.log: It takes a month. It is a very poor gate. It stands on a bare rock on the windward side with nothing behind it, and over the next century people come to leave things there, and you never did find out why.

events.text: Recorder Seol Myeongha comes with a case of measuring-rods, three clerks and a very thin smile. The Jade Court has kept a Register of Forms for eleven thousand years, ever since two forms disagreed over the Ninth Isle and there stopped being a Ninth Isle. "Purely a matter of record," says the Recorder, unrolling a chart with your name at the top. "The height, the reach, the temper. One signs here."

choices.text: Stand still and be measured

effects.log: It takes eleven days. The clerks have to go up on a kite. The Recorder writes down {dhf_size} and adds a remark you are not shown. You are on the rolls now, with duties, and everyone knows what you can do. They treat you very civilly.

choices.text: Decline, politely, and offer the Recorder tea

effects.log: The Recorder accepts the tea. "Unregistered," says the Recorder, writing it down, without any change of expression. "There is a column for that. It is a long column, and I have outlived a great many entries in it."

choices.text: Let them measure, and arrange for the rods to read a little short

ok.log: It is the most difficult conversation you have ever had with a kite. The Register now holds a modest figure against your name, and three clerks owe you a favour, and nobody will know how far it reaches until it is too late for them.

fail.log: The Recorder takes the rod out of the clerk's hand, looks at it, and hands it back. "Eleven more days," says the Recorder. And it is, and you are on the rolls with a remark that you are shown, this time.

events.text: The Recorder of the Jade Court is at a loss, and not used to it. "It has no reach," says Seol Myeongha, reading what the kite-clerks brought back. "It does not advance. It has raised a hand. Three clerks felt quite ashamed up there, and cannot say why." The thin smile comes and goes. "I shall have to rule a new column. Nobody can tell me what it is that you are keeping out."

choices.text: "Write down: a gate"

effects.log: The Recorder writes it down. "A gate to what?" You do not know. "I see," says Seol Myeongha, and for some time afterwards you get long, polite letters from the Jade Court, asking whether you have found out yet.

choices.text: "Leave it out. It is not for your book"

effects.log: "Everything is for my book," says the Recorder, quite kindly. But the column goes unruled. You find that you are pleased, and that it is a small and human sort of pleasure, up here.

events.text: They do it on the Long Terrace, with an audience. The isle-champion Oh Cheonbi has held it for six hundred years and is as bored as a person can be, with a form the size of a thunderhead drifting behind like an old dog. "It is the custom," the champion says. "The new ones raise it. Then we see how much of it was noise." The rafts are three deep, and people are selling little cakes.

choices.text: Raise it. See how much of it was noise

ok.log: The cakes stop. {dhf_Form} leans into the thunderhead and the thunderhead gives. Oh Cheonbi is smiling for the first time in six centuries, on the floor. "Oh, good," the champion says. "Do come back. Bring all of it next time."

fail.log: You spend the rest of the afternoon in a bed of cloud with a clear view of the sky. Oh Cheonbi comes and sits by you and eats a cake. "Most of it was noise," the champion says. "Not all. That is better than most. Come back in a century."

choices.text: Bow and say you did not come up here to entertain anyone

effects.log: A small, satisfied groan goes through the rafts. "That is a different custom," Oh Cheonbi says. "That one is called losing face. I rather respect it." The cake-sellers do well anyway.

events.text: Oh Cheonbi has heard about the gate. The champion floats to your bare rock, thunderhead and all, sits on the driftwood and asks to be let in. "In to what?" you say. "That's what I've come to see." The great form looms and leans on yours. It does not push. It leans, as a big person leans on a door to see if it is locked. You feel it in your teeth. It would be easy to lean back.

choices.text: Do nothing at all. Let it lean

effects.log: It leans for nine days. You make tea. On the tenth, the champion gets up, rubbing one shoulder. "Nothing," says Oh Cheonbi. "There is nothing in there. There is nothing in there, and I could not get in." The champion goes away looking happier than anyone has seen in centuries.

choices.text: Lean back

ok.log: The thunderhead goes back across the sea, a little at a time, and the champion goes with it, whooping. You have won, and the gold is looking down at you, with its hand raised. You have the feeling that you have let something in.

fail.log: The driftwood gate is all over the sea, and you with it. It takes you a year to find all the pieces. Oh Cheonbi helps, as it happens, and is not very good at it.

events.text: You nearly miss the isle: a hut, and an old immortal called Ma Hyeonseong mending a net where there are no fish. Nothing stands behind him at all. Up here that is like meeting a person with no face. "Mine broke," he says, biting off the twine. "High as a watchtower, and it knew my name. I asked it for one thing too many. Sit down. Yours wants to see this. They always do."

choices.text: Sit, and ask what he asked it for

effects.log: He tells you. It takes a long time, and at the end you would not have done any differently, and that is the worst of it. You go away with your hands cold. Behind you the form walks more carefully than it did, as you would on ice.

choices.text: Ask him how it feels now

effects.log: "Quiet," he says, after thinking it over. "I can hear the net." He does not look at you. You stay a season and help him with it, and neither of you catches a fish, and you think about that often.

choices.text: Keep walking. Whatever this is, you don't want it near you

effects.log: You get back on your raft. He does not look up. All the way home you can feel something at your back looking over its shoulder at that little hut, the way a horse looks at a butcher's yard.

events.text: Two immortals of the Eastern Chain fell out over a boundary stone and each raised a form over it, forty years ago. Neither will lower first. Under them, nine small isles have not seen daylight since, and the fishers there have gone pale and very polite. They send you a delegation in a boat, and a dried fish. It is the best fish they have got.

choices.text: Raise yours between them, and stand there until one of them gets tired

ok.log: It takes eleven years. You stand on the boundary stone with your form up and your arms shaking. It is the most boring heroism in the history of the Isles. One morning, both of them lower theirs and look away, as if they had just happened to do it. It is daylight. You are given another fish.

fail.log: After six years something gives, and it is you. They have stopped being angry with each other. They are both quite annoyed with you. The fishers help you into the boat, and they do not ask for the fish back.

choices.text: Invoke your entry: a registered form may order a boundary cleared

effects.log: You serve the notice yourself, with your line from the Register read out over the water. Both forms come down in a morning, sulking. It is daylight. It is also a debt: the Recorder notes that you have now used the Register, and the Register will remember being used.

choices.text: Take it to the Jade Court, as a question of record

effects.log: It will be heard in only ninety years. Recorder Seol Myeongha gives you a very nice receipt. You send the fishers some lamps.

choices.text: Take the fish and say it is a hard thing, and go

effects.log: It is an extremely good fish. You think about that a lot.

events.text: Your meditation on {dhf_form} has reached the place everyone comes to, and it is not written down. It has your stance and your bad habit of the left heel. It also has the whole weight of a law of the world behind it, and it was there long before you. The question is quite simple. When it rises, whose is it? Which of you is standing behind which?

choices.text: It is the law. You are only the place it came in by

effects.log: You say it aloud, and something goes out of your shoulders. It is a great relief, and a little like dying, and from then on when it rises it falls with the whole force of a thing that was always going to be true.

choices.text: It is you. It has your left heel. The law can find its own

effects.log: You say it, and it turns its head, and it looks very nearly amused. From then on when it rises, some of it stays behind to see that you are all right. It is not a very lawful thing to do. It is what you would have done.

choices.text: Refuse the question. Go and see about lunch

effects.log: You go and see about lunch. It is fine. The question will be there when you get back. It has got nothing but time.

events.text: A dry little immortal from the Scholars' Chain has read about your gate and comes to argue. "Guardians were invented by mortals," she says, sitting on your rock, "to frighten other mortals. You keep a door on a house you left a very long way down." She takes out a little abacus. She is enjoying herself, and you find you do not mind.

choices.text: "Yes. Somebody ought to keep it, though"

effects.log: She stops the abacus. She looks at you for some time, as if you had done a sum that she will have to check. She comes back every few decades after that, and the arguing is the best thing that happens on that rock.

choices.text: Ask her what she thinks is on the other side

effects.log: She starts to answer, and stops, and takes rather a long time putting away her abacus. "Well, that is a rude question," she says. It is the only rude question she has been asked in nine thousand years, and she writes it down to keep.

events.text: A thing comes up from below by the slow post, the one for prayers and very long grudges: a small square banner, sure and dry, much handled. A square person, nearly dead, has painted what could be seen from there, a smudge on a ridge with the left shoulder correct. On the back, in a child's hand: DAL SAYS YOU WILL WANT THIS. WE DO THE BRIDGE NOW.

choices.text: Hang it on the wall of your hut

effects.log: It is a small thing to hang up, among immortals. The ones who visit you do not mention it, and they look at it for quite a long time when they think you are not looking.

choices.text: Send something down, by the same post

effects.log: You send down the best blue that can be had on the Isles. It will take a hundred years to get there. It occurs to you, as the post goes down, that there will be a child there who has not been born yet who is going to know what to do with it.

events.text: Looking down through a gap in the cloud-sea, you see a small province having a bad winter, and something tall over one of its ridges, the way a thing looks from very far off. They have made a festival of it. They think it is a mountain spirit that likes rice cakes. You look behind you. {dhf_Form} has its head on one side.

choices.text: Let it be a mountain spirit, to them

effects.log: They go on with the rice cakes. A little of the bad weather goes around that ridge from then on, as it happens. You have no idea how that was done. You check, and you find it has a rather pleased look.

choices.text: Tell the Recorder the shadow is out of bounds

effects.log: "How thoughtful," says the Recorder. A form's shadow falling on the world below is a matter for a minor clerk. The clerk sees to it. The ridge has a very ordinary winter after that, and rather a bad spring.

events.text: A boy from the hidden isle brings you a mended net. Ma Hyeonseong has lain down on the shore and stopped mending, and you are in his instructions: the net, and three words on a shell. ASK IT NOTHING. You stand at evening with the net in your hands. You know what you were about to ask for. It would have been a good thing, and it would have worked.

choices.text: Do not ask. Hang the net up by the door

effects.log: It is a very hard thing not to do, on some evenings. It stands behind you and waits to be asked, and you do not ask, and you go in to supper. There is no reward. You have looked.

choices.text: Ask it anyway. He was weaker than you

effects.log: You ask. It does it, instantly, and it is all that you hoped. There is a small sound, afterwards, somewhere very high up, like the sound of a hair crack running through a cold bowl. Nothing else happens. Yet.

events.text: You had been calling it a shade, and so had everyone, with a certain tact. This morning the thin smoky thing you brought up from below has found out what it was a shade of. {dhf_Form} stands there, {dhf_look}, and looks down with what you would take, in anyone else, for relief at having finally got dressed. Across the water the old pipe-smoker looks, and goes back to her pipe.

choices.text: Tell it that it took its time

effects.log: It does not answer. You did not expect it to. But you feel the whole enormous weight of it settle more comfortably on its heels, as a person does who has been standing a long time in somebody else's shoes.

choices.text: Walk it round the isle, to get used to it

effects.log: You walk it round. You have to mind the eaves. By evening you have stopped ducking, and most of your neighbours have stopped pretending they were just on their way somewhere.

events.text: You told it once that it was the law, and you only the door it came in by. Word has reached the Jade Court. Seol Myeongha comes in person, with no kite. "Your form has been cited. As a precedent. It was ruled that what stands behind you is simply so." The thin smile does not come. "Nobody in the Register can bring a complaint against you now. I am not sure you should be pleased."

choices.text: Ask to read the case

effects.log: You read it, all nine thousand pages. There is a woman in it, and a boundary, and a boy who was in the wrong place. Nobody in it did anything wrong. You had not thought that you would mind so much, being correct.

choices.text: Thank the Recorder, and go on being the law

effects.log: "Yes," says Seol Myeongha. "I rather thought you would." The case is entered. There are a great many others after it, and none of them ever comes to your door, and it is very quiet on your isle.

events.text: You told it once that it was you, with your left heel, and that the law could find its own. The Jade Court has noticed. "A form is a law of the world," says Seol Myeongha, over your tea. "Yours held a raft for an old woman last spring. It moved out of a child's light. There is no column for that, and it is a very poor way to hold a Dao." The thin smile. "Two of my clerks have asked how it is done."

choices.text: Tell them: you go on keeping your heel

effects.log: You tell them, for what it is worth. The clerks go home thoughtful. In a few hundred years there is a small and very unofficial habit among the junior staff of holding rafts.

choices.text: Say it cannot be taught, and pour the Recorder more tea

effects.log: The Recorder drinks it, and for the first time in your acquaintance stays for a second cup. Nothing is written down. It is the highest honour the Jade Court has.

events.text: You went to see about lunch, some centuries back. The question has waited. This evening {dhf_form} has lowered itself to the height of your window and is looking in. You finish your soup. It goes on looking. It has got nothing but time, and you have run out of other things to do. When it rises, whose is it?

choices.text: The law's. You are only the place it came in by

effects.log: You say it, between mouthfuls. It straightens up and goes back out to its place, and from then on it falls with the force of a thing that was always going to be true.

choices.text: Yours. It has your left heel

effects.log: You say it with your mouth full. It looks very nearly amused. From then on, when it rises, a little of it stays behind to see that you are all right.

choices.text: Pass it the salt

effects.log: You hold out the salt to it, through the window. It considers this for about a hundred years. The students who come to you later call it the deepest answer in the Isles, and you do not correct them.

events.text: The dry little immortal from the Scholars' Chain comes to your rock for the last time, with her abacus, walking badly. She has done the sum. "It is not keeping anything out," she says. "I was wrong, and I checked. It is keeping a place. A gate is how you tell someone there is a way back." She sits down on the driftwood. "I should like it noted that this took me nine thousand years."

choices.text: Note it. Cut it into the gatepost, badly

effects.log: You cut it in with a borrowed knife. She corrects your figures. She stays until evening, and then the rock has only you on it, and the post, and the gold, looking at the door with a little more interest than before.

choices.text: Ask her who it is keeping a place for

effects.log: "Well, that is a rude question," she says, delighted, and tells you she does not know. She leaves you the abacus. You have never been able to make it come out the way she did.

events.text: The kite-clerks have come back again, although no one sent for them, and they look unwell. {dhf_Form} has grown past the mark, and past the next mark: it is {dhf_size}. When you walk across the isle now the raft-traffic parts ahead of you, and the old pipe-smoker on the point has moved her chair. Seol Myeongha sends a note in a very clean hand: AMEND YOUR ENTRY. Below the note, in a much smaller hand: Well done.

choices.text: Send an honest figure

effects.log: The entry is amended. There are two or three immortals now who have stopped being polite to you, and it is a great relief. They are the only ones that you will have to watch.

choices.text: Send no figure at all

effects.log: You will get another note. There will be a number of them. You find that you have a place for them, under the leg of the table.

events.text: One morning there is a good deal more gold. It has not got angrier, and the hand is still raised. But there are ranks of them, going back and up the sky, all with the same long-suffering face, all looking at a door. Part of the Isles has started bowing without knowing it. The rafts pass your rock very quietly, and the driftwood gate, a very poor gate, has somehow not fallen down.

choices.text: Mend the gate. It needs it

effects.log: You mend the gate, with twine, badly. It takes about a week, and you are entirely at peace. All those ranks of gold watch you get the knot wrong, with endless patience.

choices.text: Tell the bowing people to stop

effects.log: You tell them. They bow to you for telling them. You go back in and shut the door, and you can hear the small sound of someone out there laying down a dried fish.

events.text: It has come to a head. With every level of your Dao, the law has been leaning on the old gold from inside. It would be taller and truer if you let that shape go and let the Dao stand up in its own likeness. Only a guardian stands there, hand raised, looking past you. It would not stop you. That has never been what it does.

choices.text: Keep the gate

effects.log: You keep it. You will never quite be sure why. The law goes on leaning, and the gold goes on standing there, a little taller for it than it was. You sweep something, and feel better.

choices.text: Let it go, with thanks, and let the Dao stand

effects.log: You bow to it, properly, for the first time since you were young. It does not bow. It looks away from the door, once, down at you, and it is not possible to say what is in that look. Then there is no gold, and what rises there instead is very great indeed.

events.text: Nobody tells you this happens up here. You have had an extremely bad decade. This morning the cloud-sea below your isle has gone the colour of a bruise, in the exact outline of {dhf_form}, and your neighbour has sent a clerk to ask if you are quite well. It is looking at you. You had thought that happened to other people.

choices.text: Stop fighting it. A law does not have to be kind

effects.log: You stop. It is so restful. The sea stays that colour. Your neighbour moves, a whole isle, over the course of a year, and you do not trouble to see where.

choices.text: Go and sit on the shore with the bruise, and stay until it clears

effects.log: It takes nine years, and it hurts all the way. You think of very little except the sea. When it is over, you have an excellent understanding of how close that was, and you do not tell your neighbour.

events.text: Someone has left a dried fish at your gate and it has gone black. They all have, the whole row of them. You look behind you and the gold is the colour of a pot that has been left on a fire. There are ranks of them up the sky, and they have turned around. They are looking at you now. They look at you the way they looked at that door. You understand, rather late, what it was that they were keeping out.

choices.text: So be it. A closed fist holds a gate as well as an open hand

effects.log: You raise your own fist, and all that burnt gold does the same. The Isles go quiet. There will be no more fish. You did not much care for fish.

choices.text: Go out and clean the row, fish by fish, with your own hands

effects.log: It takes a very long time and nobody thanks you. You scrub the driftwood and mend the knot. When at last you look up, the nearest rank has turned its head back towards the door. There are a great many more ranks.

events.text: They have stopped sending clerks. Your name has moved in the Register, from one column to a much shorter one, and you have heard from an unusually polite visitor that there has been some discussion of a hearing. {dhf_Form} has grown a habit. When you are thinking of something else, it leans over the sea and looks down at the world below through the gap, patiently, like a child looking into a nest.

choices.text: Pull it back, every time, however long it takes

effects.log: You get very little else done. It is like holding a door shut against a slow steady tide. But it comes away from the gap, and the nest below goes on being a nest.

choices.text: Have a look yourself. What can it hurt

effects.log: You have a look. It is all very small down there. You had forgotten how small. It is hard to recall why you used to mind.

events.text: A very junior clerk is on your doorstep in some alarm. Your line in the Register has changed by itself: under TEMPER, the ink has simply gone, and the Recorder would like to know what you have done. You look out at the sea of cloud, plain and boring white. {dhf_Form} stands behind you, looking at it too. You offer the clerk some tea, and find you have a good deal to say about the weather.

choices.text: Tell the Recorder the truth: you sat

effects.log: You write one line. A reply comes in a very clean hand, in rather less time than these things usually take. It says only: So did I, once. Do not tell anyone.

choices.text: Tell the Recorder it is none of the Court's affair

effects.log: It is entered as Unknown. It is a very small triumph, and you are a very long way up, and you enjoy it more than you would have believed.

events.text: It takes the isle's physician a season to work out what happened to you. She sits by your bed with an old book open. "Self-inflicted, is the entry. You raised it and it looked down. It says it is not a form of attack, strictly. It is a form of opinion." She looks over your shoulder, where it stands in great calm, and shuts the book. "I shall need paying before you get up."

choices.text: Pay her, and start sitting with it the day you can stand

effects.log: She takes the stones and goes, quite quickly. You begin the day you can stand. It lets you. That is not at all the same as it being on your side.

choices.text: Ask the book how to make it mean it next time

effects.log: She looks at you for a moment. Then she gives you the book and does not ask for it back, and she goes down the road without looking round.

events.text: {npc} has not missed a day of your long life. {He} comes across the cloud-sea on foot at first light, and behind {him}, to the top of the sky, walks {dhf_rival}. Rafts turn back from far off. The Recorder has sent a very small clerk to witness, who is being sick over the side of a kite. "We've got the room," {npc} says happily. "Let's see them do it properly. Then it's done, for every life."

choices.text: Raise {dhf_form} and let them settle every life at once

ok.log: It takes a year. There is weather from it on isles no one has charted. When it stops, {dhf_form} is standing, and the sea has a long new valley in it. {npc} comes up out of the cloud and bows, all the way down, as if {he} had been practising for it since you were six. "It is over," {he} says. "I will not be born beside you again." The very small clerk writes it down.

fail.log: The sea closes over your head. {npc} fishes you out, and props you against a rock, and looks at you for a good while. "No," {he} says. "That was not all of you. I know the difference. I have seen all of you. Come and find me, when you have got it."

choices.text: Lower it. Walk out to meet {him} with nothing behind you

mem.note: lowered a form on the cloud-sea

effects.log: It is a long walk on cloud. {He} waits, with that great thing standing at {his} back, and when you get there, {he} looks at you for some time. "You always did know how to spoil an occasion," {he} says. The knot is still there. But the very small clerk has stopped being sick.

choices.text: "Another century, I think"

effects.log: "Fine," {he} says, and sits down on the sea. "I brought a book." {He} is still there when you get home, and you can see {him} from the window, reading.

events.text: A raft ties up at your isle, old and badly kept. {npc} has time now there is nothing between you, and has gone to some trouble to look as if {he} was just passing. {He} accepts tea. "I've been wondering what would happen if they tried to look at each other from the same side. I don't suppose you've got a century?" Far off, a shape leans into the sky, trying to look casual.

choices.text: Have them try it. And then have them fight, of course

ok.log: It starts with looking and, by the second decade, it is what it always was. The neighbours complain. You win, as far as anyone can tell, and {npc} complains about that for a further hundred years, and the two of you agree that it was a very good century.

fail.log: You come round on {his} raft, heading nowhere much. "I took some of your good tea," {he} says, "as an indemnity." It has been a great many lives since you had such a good time losing.

choices.text: Put the two of them side by side and go fishing

effects.log: You do not catch anything. There are no fish. You both know that. There are two very tall shapes against the evening behind you, looking the same way, and it is the most peaceful thing you have seen on the Isles.

events.text: A god's form has nowhere to stand that is not already somebody's. You find this out on your first morning in the Divine Realm, when {dhf_form} goes up with nothing under it, like a hanged banner. Gods turn their heads with mild interest. An old surveyor with a knotted cord stops at your gate. "You'll want a domain to put that on," he says. "Or it won't be any good to anyone."

choices.text: Ask how much it would take to fill it

effects.log: Surveyor Daeyeon looks at it for a long time and takes the cord from his shoulder. "How much have you got?" he says. He has a way of asking it that you will come to know.

choices.text: Lower it, and hope nobody saw

effects.log: Everybody saw. They are only gods, and they have nothing else to look at. But they will take your modesty into account, and it may even be a thousand years before it comes up at a dinner.

events.text: A god of the Golden Field is showing you around, bored. You pass the old gate of the Hall, which has no doors and no doorkeeper and has not needed one for an age. {dhf_Form} rises behind you unasked, and goes and stands in it. The god stops talking. A number of very large beings on their way to lunch have to stop and go around.

choices.text: Call it back, and apologise

effects.log: It comes when called. You apologise to several gods. They take it well, but you see one or two of them looking at that empty gateway, afterwards, as though they had never given it a thought before now, and did not altogether like to.

choices.text: Leave it there a moment. See what it does

effects.log: It does nothing. It stands there, with one hand raised, for most of a century, and in all of that time nobody quite wants to ask you to move it. You have an idea that you have got somebody's attention. It is not at all clear whose.

events.text: Surveyor Daeyeon walks the bounds of what you hold, eighty years on foot with his cord and a bad hip. He is the only one in the Realm not afraid to tell a god how much they have got. "You are {dhf_size}," he says at your gate, knocking mud off a boot. "It stands on what you hold, and what you hold stands on who minds you holding it. Do you know who minds?"

choices.text: Ask him to tell you who

effects.log: He tells you, all of them, in order, with the distances. It takes a whole evening. He is a very restful man to have a list of your enemies from. You give him a better pair of boots.

choices.text: Tell him it does not matter who minds

effects.log: "No," says Daeyeon. "That is what the last one said," and he nods towards a piece of the horizon where nothing is. He takes his cord and goes. You find that you look over that way more often than you would like.

events.text: Surveyor Daeyeon comes to walk the bounds, stops after a week, and sits on your step with one boot off. "It does not have any," he says. "This thing has a hand up, and on that side there's your ground, and on that side something else. I walked along it seven days and I don't know what it's dividing." He looks into the boot. "What are you holding it shut against?"

choices.text: Say you have been asked before, and you still do not know

effects.log: "Hm," says Daeyeon. He stays for three days to look at it. When he goes, he leaves behind a short length of his cord, knotted off, on your step, and neither of you mentions that.

choices.text: Ask him to walk it with you, and see

effects.log: You walk it with him. It takes a decade, and you talk mostly about boots. At the end of it neither of you knows any more, and he has become the only person in the Realm who calls you by your name.

events.text: It turns out that it has a shadow. A plain far below lies under your form for part of each day now. The priests there note a late spring, a thin harvest, then a thinner one. Nobody down there knows what it is. They think they have done something wrong. You have a very clear view of them working out what it could have been. They have started on their own children's faults.

choices.text: Draw the form in. Let it be smaller, for them

effects.log: It is the hardest thing you have done since the gate. It is like breathing out and holding it, all day, every day, for ever. The other gods notice. They say nothing to you. They begin to treat you as someone who is smaller. The plain gets a good harvest.

choices.text: Move your seat, so it falls on a sea

effects.log: You move. It costs you a very good view and some standing with a storm-god who owned the sea. Well: now they have got a slow cold fishing year on the coast. But nobody is blaming their children.

choices.text: They will adapt. Things do

effects.log: They adapt. They become a pale, patient, careful people who plant barley, and they build their houses with no windows on the side you are on. They are said to be very polite.

events.text: A priest called Ongnye has come up from the plain by a road the gods thought was closed. It took most of her life. She is small and furious, walks straight past your guardians, looks up at {dhf_form} and raises one finger. "You. I don't want a blessing. My mother died of your shadow. I want it written down that it was you, and I want you to look at me when you do it."

choices.text: Look at her. Write it down in your own hand

effects.log: It takes a long time to write it all down, and she checks your spelling of the names. When you have finished she folds it and goes home, without thanking you, by the same road. She lives to be very old, and the plain remembers, and you are not forgiven, and it is right.

choices.text: Offer her what a god can offer: long life, a good harvest

effects.log: "I told you," she says. She does not raise her voice. She goes back down the road. Her people plant no barley on your account after that, not any more. They burn your name in a small way, every autumn, and it does not hurt. You have looked into that, and it does not.

choices.text: Have her shown out

effects.log: She is shown out. She is shown out very respectfully. Nobody can quite recall afterwards how she had got in. When you check that road, you find it is closed. It was always closed.

events.text: Ongnye, a small furious priest, comes up from the plain by the closed road, walks past all your attendants, and stops in front of the gold with her mouth open. "My mother had one of those on a little banner," she says at last. "For the fever. It looked just like that." She goes on looking up. "I came here to shout at you. Who is it stopping? Do you know that we prayed to that?"

choices.text: Tell her the truth: it has never answered you either

effects.log: She laughs, and it is not a pleasant sound, and then she sits down on the floor and looks old. You sit down too. You talk till evening about her mother, and she goes home by the same road.

choices.text: Raise it for her at full height, so she can see what they prayed to

effects.log: She looks for a long time. "It is not looking at me," she says. "It never was, was it. It was looking at what was behind me." She seems to come to some decision about that. Later you hear that the plain has a new kind of festival, very quiet, with all the doors left open.

events.text: The border god Sangwi has a form like a slow tide of black horses. Nobody has declared anything. The horses only graze a little further over each decade. Surveyor Daeyeon stands at your side with his cord, looking very tired. "You can have it out, or give him the valley, or go to the Hall and complain. All of those have been done. I have the figures."

choices.text: Stand {dhf_form} on the border, and have it out

ok.log: The horses come on for nine days. On the tenth, they mill and turn. Sangwi comes to the line and takes off a glove and says something courteous. It is an excellent treaty. Daeyeon knots his cord in the old place, and the valley people never find out they were in a war.

fail.log: You hold on longer than anyone expected. Sangwi is gracious. It is only a valley. Daeyeon moves your mark with his own hands, and he does not say anything, and he comes to supper.

choices.text: Give him the valley, in writing, and keep your own hands clean

effects.log: Sangwi sends a very fine present. He will want the next valley in about a thousand years. Daeyeon looks at you for some time and writes it down.

choices.text: Ride out alone, and ask him what the horses want

effects.log: He is so astonished that he tells you. It takes all night, and you are both hoarse by the end of it. They do not want anything. They have only ever been told to go forward. He stares at them for quite a while. The grazing slows, somewhat.

events.text: A child has got into your domain. Her name is Bom, she is about seven, she is from the plain, and she has climbed one of {dhf_form}'s feet by a route you would not have thought there was. She sits on the instep with a cold, kicking her heels. She would like to know if it gets tired. Her father is a carter and he gets tired, and no one asks him.

choices.text: Tell her yes. Sit down with her on the instep

effects.log: You sit. You had not known that it was true until you said it. She gives you half a rice ball, a bad one. You send her home on a bird with a good coat and no blessings, because you can see what those do. Then you sit a while longer.

choices.text: Tell her gods do not get tired, and send her home

effects.log: She looks at you with a great deal of pity, as she would a carter who says the same. She goes home on a bird. You find it stays with you, that look, for rather longer than the wars have.

choices.text: Ask her to ask it herself

effects.log: She shouts it up, with both hands. There is a long pause of the kind that you get with very tall things. Then, over the whole of your domain, for about as long as it takes to breathe, it sits down. It is talked about for ten thousand years. Nobody at the Hall can say what it meant.

events.text: Your pantheon has sent for it, not so plainly. There is a war, or the sort of dispute held with armies, and a very elegant envoy says {dhf_form} is greatly admired. It need only stand on the eastern line, {dhf_size}, where the enemy's priests can see it, and their people, and their people's children. They are sure you understand how much that would save in the long run.

choices.text: Go, and stand it on the line, and let it do its work

effects.log: It does its work. Three pantheon armies and a province of the world below turn around and go home, with hardly a blow. It is a very merciful victory. Nobody on that side of the line sleeps well for a century, and they teach their children to.

choices.text: Refuse. It is not a banner

effects.log: The envoy looks only mildly disappointed. It will be a thing that they remember. A good many things become slightly more difficult for you from then on, and the war goes on for two hundred years.

choices.text: Go, but go in front of it, with your own hands, and fight like anyone

effects.log: You go down the line on foot. It stays home. Everyone on your own side is extremely annoyed. On the other side, they tell a story about it, and it is not the story that the envoy would have wanted.

events.text: They want it for the eastern line. The envoy is very elegant: your guardian has a moral authority not otherwise available. It need only stand with its hand up, and the enemy will understand that heaven is closed to them. Gold looks very well on a battlefield. You look behind you. It has never looked at any of them. It seems to you that it is looking, now, at you.

choices.text: Say it does not keep that kind of gate

effects.log: "Every gate is that kind of gate," says the envoy, kindly, and you think about that a great deal in the bad years that follow. But it stays where it is, with its hand up, against something else.

choices.text: Send it. Saving lives is what it is for

effects.log: It goes. It stands on the line with its hand up and three armies stop, and it is everything the envoy promised. The gold has a dull bloom on it that was not there. You cannot get it off. You have tried.

events.text: Surveyor Daeyeon comes for the last time, carried, with the very old cord. It goes all the way around. Every mark in it was someone, every god who ever stood a form on a world, and they all come to the same length. He has never told any of them. You go out together and he looks up at it. "You might think of leaving a bit over," he says. "For whoever is underneath."

choices.text: Take the cord from him, and go and walk the bounds yourself

effects.log: It takes four hundred years. You are not very good at it. There is a bad place on the east side that you have to do three times, and when you get back you have got a limp, and you know the name of everything you are standing on.

choices.text: Thank him, and see that he lacks for nothing

effects.log: You see to it. He has a good room with a good view, for what he has left. You keep the cord in a box. Every so often, you look at it. It does not get any longer. It does not get any shorter.

events.text: A shade has no business in the Divine Realm, as helpful people have told you. You chose your Dao late, and this morning it has come through, as a late tooth does. {dhf_Form} stands up all at once, {dhf_size}, where there was smoke. Daeyeon comes by with the cord and looks at it from several sides. "You will want to get that looked at," he says, as pleased as you have ever seen him.

choices.text: Ask Daeyeon to measure it

effects.log: He measures it. It takes him the better part of forty years, and he complains the whole way round, and you bring him his dinner on the east side, where there is no road.

choices.text: Stand it up where they can all see

effects.log: They all see. A good many invitations come, and a few of them are even sincere. You had nearly forgotten what it was to be looked at in that particular way.

events.text: You told it once that it was yours, that it had your left heel, and that the law could find its own. At the end of a very bad war you lie on a field that used to be a province. Nearly all of it has gone on to the line, as a god's form must. But a small part has stayed, about as big as a person, sitting by you with its back to all of heaven. It has your bad habit of the left heel.

choices.text: Stay there with it a while

effects.log: Nobody knows where you are for a hundred years, and the Hall is in an uproar. It is the first time since you were young that anything has just sat by you with nothing to gain by it. It does not say anything either.

choices.text: Tell it to get back to the line. They need it

effects.log: It goes. It looks back once. Your pantheon wins, and it is a very great victory, and for a long time after that you find you keep moving your left foot, for no reason.

events.text: You told it once that it was the law. Down in the world they have stopped praying to {dhf_form} and started citing it. Whole peoples settle their boundaries by what falls under its shadow, and nobody asks you. Surveyor Daeyeon lays the cord on your table. There is a country, he says, where the law has been right for nine generations. He has walked it. He could not find anyone who laughed.

choices.text: Go down and rule one case wrongly, on purpose, in mercy

effects.log: A debtor, a small one. You stand in the square in borrowed shoes and find for him, against all the figures. It cracks something very old. A woman at the back of the square starts laughing, and cannot say why, and it spreads.

choices.text: Leave it. It is correct

effects.log: It is correct. Daeyeon rolls up the cord. That country goes on for a long time without a single error, and you have the figures, and they are very beautiful.

events.text: At your rank nobody asks whose it is. Then a very old carter's daughter comes up the closed road on two sticks and sits on the instep, as she did at seven, or as someone like her did. "I always wondered," she says. "That great thing. Whose is it, anyway? My father had a horse he said was his, and I never saw him tell it anything."

choices.text: "The law's. I only opened the door"

effects.log: She nods. "That is what he said about the horse," she says. It falls harder after that, with all the force of a thing that was always true, and you think of the horse more than you would have expected.

choices.text: "Mine. It has my left heel"

effects.log: She looks. "So it has," she says, as if that were the plainest thing in the Realm. From then on, when it rises, a little of it stays behind with you. It is not at all how a god is meant to do this.

choices.text: "I never saw it take an order either. Whose do you think?"

effects.log: She thinks it over for the whole afternoon, kicking one stick. "Nobody's," she decides. "It only stays." You send her home on a bird with a good coat. You find you have nothing to add.

events.text: Ages on, you go and stand beside it at last, on its own side, and look where it has always looked. You had thought a door held something terrible back from heaven. Through the draught you can see barley, a carter, a very small plain going about its day. Its raised hand is facing in. It has never faced out. All this time it has stood with its back to the world, and its hand up to the gods.

choices.text: Stand beside it, and keep your own hand up

effects.log: You stand there, a god, with one hand raised against gods. It is a very long watch. Nobody in the Hall ever works out why you stopped coming to dinner, and on the plain the barley does as it likes.

choices.text: Ask it to let you through, just once, to see

effects.log: It does not lower the hand. It does not look at you. You stay on your side, and you find, after a while, that you are not disappointed, and that this is the first time you have understood what you are for.

events.text: It happened in the night, if there is such a thing here. Messengers come all morning. The moons are mis-timed along one side of the Realm, in the shadow of {dhf_form}, and would you mind. Every god with a window has looked out of it and adjusted what they mean to say to you next. Daeyeon sends only a bit of cord, with a new knot in it.

choices.text: Apologise to the moons

effects.log: You send a note to the moons. It is the sort of thing that you can do now. Everyone agrees that it was a charming gesture from one who could so easily have made none.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let them adjust

effects.log: They adjust. There is a good deal less conversation at your table from now on. It is much more interesting, and you sleep with one eye open.

events.text: It is yours now, by every mark in the book. {dhf_Form} goes out ahead of you and puts a foot down, and you feel it take. Rivers you have never seen run for a moment with your pulse. A whole people has started dreaming about a tall shape. You are {dhf_size}. The old shrines are having their paint touched up by people who could not tell you why.

choices.text: Walk the new ground on foot, and learn its names

effects.log: It takes a long time, and you are not at all what they were expecting. A great-grandmother in a mountain village gives you a slightly stale cake, and she tells you that you look thin.

choices.text: Stand on it and let them feel it

effects.log: They feel it. It is all over very quickly: all the doors are shut, all the prayers are correct. It is such a quiet, tidy domain, once you have stood on it for a while.

events.text: You lost it, and the mark has been moved. {dhf_Form} has stepped back off the ground it stood on, and it is {dhf_size}. There is a long pale footprint across a whole country, where nothing has grown for years. The people have come out of their houses to look at the sky, the way you look at a ceiling after a large noise has stopped. A few of them have started to sing.

choices.text: Listen to the singing

effects.log: It is not a very good song. It is about the weather. You listen for all of the time that it lasts. You had thought that you would mind it more, and then you do, a good while later.

choices.text: Note down who is singing

effects.log: You note it. You have a very long memory, and time on your side. There is no hurry whatever. Behind you it has started, very slightly, to lean.

events.text: The law you have walked has grown past all measure and wants a shape it can use. The old gold fits it as a door fits a sea. Your attendants have started trying to meet its eye, and it does not look back; it looks past you at a door. At your level of things you could be anything. A great deal of power is simply standing in the hall, waiting for you to say the word.

choices.text: Keep the old gold. Somebody ought to

effects.log: You say no, again. It is a little more difficult every age. Some of the gods take it for humility, and some for a very long and subtle plan. You are not going to tell them that you have no idea.

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go at last

effects.log: You bow. Then the whole hall is full of what you have always been able to be. It is magnificent. You look for some time at the place in the doorway where nobody is standing now, and you wonder about that for the rest of your days.

events.text: On the plain, this year, all the barley has come up pointing one way. A priest there called Ongnye has sent up one line: LOOK AT YOURSELF. You look. {dhf_Form} stands where it always has, and it is smiling. It has never had a mouth. There is a pleasant, slightly hungry feeling at the back of your skull. You are a god, and there is nobody at all who could make you stop.

choices.text: Then do not stop

effects.log: You do not stop. The barley goes on pointing. Nothing else in all your domain changes, for some time. People are very careful about where they look, and they tell their children to be.

choices.text: Take it back in, as far as it goes, and sit in the dark with it

effects.log: It takes forty years, and no one can get a decision out of you for all that time, and your domain is the worse for it. When the barley stands up straight, you write one line to Ongnye. There is no reply. You had not expected any.

events.text: It has lowered its hand. In all these ages you have never seen that. The gold has gone dark as a burned pan, and the great hand holds something you cannot see, perhaps a bar. All along the edge of your domain there is a very slight draught, as if something somewhere has been left open. The Warden stands with its back to the door now, looking in at you.

choices.text: Look back. It was always going to come to this

effects.log: You look back at it. Neither of you looks away. The door stands open, behind it, and the draught goes on, and you find that it is quite easy to get used to.

choices.text: Go and shut the door yourself, whatever is on the other side

effects.log: You go past it. You would not have thought you could. You never tell anyone what you saw through there, or how long it took, or what you left behind you to get it closed. When you come back the hand is up.

events.text: A very young god has come to ask how to hold a domain. Nobody told them not to. They sit on the edge of a chair in your hall, trying not to look over your head, and the cup rattles in their hands. Your attendants have found reasons to be at the far end. You have been talking for some time, you have no idea what you have said, and it has been saying it for you.

choices.text: Stop. Send the child away. Sit with what you have heard

effects.log: You send them away. It takes a good while to remember how your own voice goes. You practise, some evenings, on the wall.

choices.text: Go on. It gives good advice

effects.log: It gives excellent advice. The young god goes home and does just as it says. You hear about it afterwards. Everyone does.

events.text: There is a song on the plain now, about how you are kind. They are made to sing it. You did not order that. Nobody gave any order, as far as you can find out. It seems the order was in the air. Your hall is exceedingly clean, your mark has moved out a good way on all sides without a single duel, and Daeyeon has sent back the boots you gave him, in a parcel, with no letter.

choices.text: Find out who ordered the song, and stop it

effects.log: You trace it all the way up. You go up a long way, and you do not much like where you get to. You stop it there, as well as you can, and you take rather a long time looking in that mirror.

choices.text: Keep the boots. It is a good song

effects.log: You keep the boots. You take to humming it. The tune is really very catchy, once you stop listening to the words.

events.text: Ongnye's granddaughter comes up the closed road with a basket, quite matter-of-fact. The barley on the plain came up every way at once this year, as barley should. The old woman said to tell you, to give you this, and not to wait for an answer. It is a small plain cake. Behind you, {dhf_form} looks at nothing again. There is a long mark on it that will not come off. You eat the cake.

choices.text: Send a word back: thank you

effects.log: She says she is not to wait for an answer, and she does not. You send it anyway, by the slow road, and it gets there about thirty years after everyone has died. They keep it in the granary. Nobody can read it.

choices.text: Keep the basket. Say nothing. Go on being careful

effects.log: You keep the basket on a shelf in the hall, among the tributes of whole worlds. The other gods take it for a very deep allusion, and they spend a long time working out what it means.

events.text: It is a very great scandal. A god has been hurt in a duel, by no one. You raised it and it looked down and, before the whole Hall, struck the one who raised it. Physicians have been sent by those who wish you well, and by those who do not. You can see it through the ceiling, behind your bed, looking calm. It looks as though it is thinking of what to do with the domain.

choices.text: Get up. Go out on the terrace, where it can see you do it
