effects.log: You get up. You should not. You go out in front of everyone, grey as a dishcloth, and you stand under it, and you sit down, and you begin. They will talk of it for a thousand years, and you will not be there to hear it, since you are sitting.

choices.text: Tell it the terms. You have got a domain, it has got your name

effects.log: It is the most interesting negotiation you have ever had. You come out of it with most of what you went in with. You do not read the small print, as there is no one left who could read it to you.

events.text: {npc} sent a note. You have both walked out past all the marks in the surveyors' cords, to a place with no ground, since nobody was ever big enough to need it. {dhf_Form} stands up and goes on standing up. Far across, {dhf_rival} does the same, {npc} very small at its feet, with a folding stool. "I thought we might want to sit down after," {he} calls. "Whichever of us it is."

choices.text: Bring it all, and finish what the two of you began when you were six

ok.log: There is a new sort of star over the Realm for a while after that. When it has cooled, {npc} is sitting on the stool, with one arm not working. {He} gets up and gives you the stool, and {he} bows, down to the place where there is no ground. "It is over," {he} says. "I will not be born beside you again." You sit. You had not expected that you would have to sit down alone.

fail.log: It goes on, and it goes wrong for you, and then there is the view from very far down. {npc} has dragged the stool over, and {he} sits by you, breathing hard. "Not that way, then," {he} says. "Not yet. I would like to have been sure that was you. Find me again."

choices.text: Walk across to {him}, and take a look at the stool

mem.note: came across the empty place with open hands

effects.log: It takes a long time, in that place. You leave it all standing behind you, and go on over with your hands open. "It is a very poor stool," you say. {He} looks at you, and at what you left behind you, and sits down on the nothing, and pats the stool. It is not over. But you have both got a seat.

choices.text: "I forgot something. Next age"

effects.log: "You did not," says {npc}, folding the stool. "But I will be here. I am not the one who has got a domain to feed."

events.text: Your attendants announce {npc} in hushed voices, then ask {him} to wipe {his} feet. There is nothing in the book between you any more. {He} has brought cards. Behind {him}, against the side of heaven, something the size of a season is trying to peer into your hall. "It missed yours," {npc} says, dealing. "Don't tell it I said."

choices.text: Put the cards down and take them outside, the way it used to be

ok.log: The Hall sends an official complaint, then a second, and then a request for tickets. It is a fine, loud, pointless century. You win, you think. {npc} says that you did not. The argument about that is the best thing that happens in the Divine Realm for some time.

fail.log: You lose very thoroughly, in front of absolutely everyone. {npc} is kind about it for as much as a whole hour. It has done your reputation a good deal of harm, and you cannot remember when you last laughed so much.

choices.text: Deal. Let them look at each other through the window

effects.log: You play cards. You are not very good, and {he} cheats, and {he} has been doing it since you were six. Outside, two enormous shapes lean together on either side of your roof, looking in at the two of you with what you could almost take for envy.

events.text: You have climbed as high as anyone in {pw_world} has climbed. You are alone on the ridge at first light when your shadow stands up taller than you and turns to look at the valley. It has long hands. It looks at the rivers one after another, as if checking them. Every child in {pw_world} knows that shape from the old temple walls, and you could not say why it makes you want to cry.

choices.text: Sit down until it goes

effects.log: You sit down and shake for a while. It does not go, exactly. It settles. All the way down, the valley seems very familiar, in a way that has nothing to do with having grown up there.

choices.text: Look where it is looking

effects.log: You look. There is a bend in the river there that has always bothered you. You could not say why. It looks as if someone meant to come back and fix it.

events.text: The Pillar-Keeper Anwi is eighty, half deaf, sixty years a sweeper of the Old Pillars, and she knows what she is seeing as you come round the bend. She drops her broom. All her life she has told the children: the Maker went away. She looks you over like a horse sold under a false name. "You are somebody's child," she says. "You have a rash on your neck. Who gave you the right to wear that?"

choices.text: "I do not know. I wish you would tell me"

effects.log: She looks at you for a long time, and something in the old face gives way, and she goes and picks up her broom. "Come and carry water," she says. "We will find out." You carry water for her for a good while, and the two of you do not find out.

choices.text: "Nobody gave it to me. It is mine"

effects.log: "That is what I was afraid of," she says, quite quietly. She picks up the broom. By the next festival, it is known in all the villages that the Pillar-Keeper will not have you on her steps.

choices.text: Bow, say nothing, and go on down the road

effects.log: You go on. When you look back, from the turn, she has not moved. There is something behind you, and it has looked back too, very gently, and she has gone down on both knees in the dust and it is the very last thing she wants to be doing.

events.text: A carver named Tesu is cutting the Maker's likeness into the cliff above the river town, three lives' work, paid for in turnips. Tesu comes down the scaffold, looks past you, goes pale, then very angry. "The hands are too long. Sixty generations have been told that's a mistake in the old style. It's not a mistake, is it? Stand there. Don't move."

choices.text: Stand there, as long as it takes

effects.log: You stand there all summer. The town gets used to it and starts to bring you turnips. The cliff has hands now such as nobody has ever carved. You catch yourself looking at them with a feeling that you cannot account for at all, a kind of embarrassment.

choices.text: Tell Tesu to leave the hands as they were. It is better that way

effects.log: Tesu stares at you, and goes on staring, and climbs back up, and leaves the hands as they were. You think that it was kind. You go on thinking so for some time. Tesu never does speak to you again.

choices.text: Move on before anyone else looks past you

effects.log: You move on. You can see the cliff for three days down the road. You can see that someone up there has stopped working, and is looking after you, the whole time.

events.text: It was bound to happen. The hill towns have it all worked out: the Maker has come home in the body of somebody's child, and all the taxes are cancelled. Three hundred of them are on the road below your house, singing, with their children and their goats. The Keepers have sent word to the king. There are horsemen coming, and nobody down there carries anything sharper than a hoe.

choices.text: Go down and tell them all to go home: you are not who they think

effects.log: You tell them, at some length, standing on a cart. They are very moved by your humility. Some of them weep. A good many go home with the news that you said so, which proves it. It is the best that you can do, and the horsemen arrive to find a much smaller crowd.

choices.text: Raise it over the road, so the horsemen stop

effects.log: The horsemen stop. All the horses and the people, the whole valley, stop, and look up. Then they kneel, with their goats. Nobody will ever go home again, or pay any tax to anyone. That was not what you meant. It may be a very long time before it matters what you meant.

choices.text: Slip away by night, and draw the horsemen after you

ok.log: You lead them through the marshes for a month and lose them in the reeds. The singers wake up to find you gone, and they are grieved, and they go home. It is the first thing that you have done which you are sure was yours.

fail.log: They catch you at the ford and you take a bad beating before they find out who you are. Then they find out, and you would give a great deal to have the beating back. The captain is very apologetic. He has brought his mother.

events.text: You keep having the same dream: you are very large and very bored, doing something careful with your long hands among many small lights, while someone stands by with a list. You wake with a word for a stone no one in {pw_world} has ever found, and you know where to dig for it. You stop by the river. That bend still bothers you. You know now how you would fix it, and that you could.

choices.text: Fix the bend

effects.log: You raise it, at dawn, with no one watching, and the long hands go down, and you feel the whole weight of the world shift very slightly and settle. It is much better. Forty villages find that their wells have moved. You did not think about the wells. Someone used to hold a list.

choices.text: Leave it. Whoever did that had reasons, or did not

effects.log: You leave it. You go home. It goes on bothering you, every day of your life, as it was evidently always going to. You catch yourself feeling very sorry for somebody, a long way off and a long time ago, who had a great deal to do.

choices.text: Go and ask Anwi who it was that held the list

effects.log: She stops sweeping. It is the first time you have ever seen her afraid. "That is not in any of the prayers," she says. "Who told you there was a list?" You stay on that day, and carry the water, and the two of you do not speak of it again.

events.text: Anwi the Pillar-Keeper is dying and has sent for you. They have carried her out to the steps to see the Pillars. "I hated you," she says finally. "Sixty years I swept for someone who went away, and you turned up with a rash." Her hand is a bundle of dry sticks. "If you are in there, somewhere under the rash: I would like you to know that we kept the place very clean."

choices.text: "I know you did. Thank you." Whether or not it is true

effects.log: You do not know who said that. It came out in your own voice. Her face does something that you would not have thought it could still do. She dies around noon, and you take up the broom, since nobody tells you not to.

choices.text: Raise it, here on the steps, for her to see

effects.log: It goes up, past the tops of the Pillars, and it looks down at the small old woman, and it bends. You did not tell it to. For as long as it takes her to stop breathing, the long hands are held around those steps as you shelter a flame. Then it stands up again, and it does not seem to know you.

choices.text: "I am only somebody's child. I am sorry"

effects.log: "Yes," she says. "So I told them." She seems satisfied. She looks at the Pillars until she stops. You sit a good while, and you are not certain what it is that you have refused.

events.text: It is {dhf_size} now, and things have begun to happen. Old relics in {pw_world} hum in their boxes when you pass. The Keepers have ruled this a coincidence and sent a clerk to follow you. Animals found nowhere else come down from the high places, look at you, sit a while and go. You know the names of a good many stones. You have stopped telling people, since it upsets them.

choices.text: Keep walking. Tell the clerk the names, if asked

effects.log: The clerk writes them down with a shaking hand, and later, in a small way, gets rich.

choices.text: Go up to where the animals go, and see what they have been looking at

effects.log: It is only a bare place, high up, with a very good view. You sit in it. It is a tired sort of feeling, and you stay until you have to come down to eat.

events.text: A dog bit you in a village, and you looked at it. You did not decide to. Going back that evening, you find the whole dog-line gone and the villagers very polite. Your shadow's long hands have closed. You know this feeling: you spent a long time making something, it came out wrong, and it has started to answer back. There is a clean way to deal with that. You can feel all of it in your hands.

choices.text: It is your world. Do what you like with it

effects.log: It is your world. That is not a thing anyone could ever say out loud, down here. You do not say it. But the people along the road have started to get off it well before you come, and they will not look up, and they have started to pray in a different way.

choices.text: Go and find out what became of the dogs, and the people who kept them

effects.log: You walk back. You stay till spring, in that village, and you do what can be done, which is not much. They have got a new litter by then. One of the pups bites you. You look at the ground very carefully, and you let it.

events.text: The cliff is finished, by Tesu or Tesu's grandchild, and it is the first thing you see coming down into the river town. The long hands are open. They could have been made another way. A little girl who has no idea who you are takes your sleeve to get a better look. Behind you the air is only air, with something large and quiet in it. Its hands have opened too. They have been for a while.

choices.text: Buy a turnip

effects.log: It is a very ordinary turnip, and it is the best you have ever eaten. You wonder who thought of it. You have a feeling that it may have been quite an afterthought.

choices.text: Stay, and tell the child what the carving is

effects.log: You tell her it is the Maker. She looks at it for a bit. "Why does it look sorry?" she says. You are not able to tell her that. You buy her a turnip.
